In 2024, the latest year available, about **12.8%** of Alberta children under 18 were in poverty. That uses the Market Basket Measure (MBM, 2023 base), Canada's official poverty line.

- Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0135-01, vector v1792632015 (percentage of persons under 18 in low income, Alberta). It was released 2026-04-29.
- Trend: the rate was 11.9% in 2023, 12.0% in 2022, 8.1% in 2021 and 4.6% in 2020. The 2020 and 2021 figures were lower, likely reflecting pandemic income supports.
- Alternative measure: on the Low Income Measure after tax (LIM-AT), the 2024 rate was **13.9%** (v96520326, same table).

The two measures differ in method, so the rates are not directly comparable.

In 2025, employees in Alberta's public administration earned an average of **$46.96 per hour** and **$1,773.90 per week**. These figures cover full- and part-time employees of all genders, aged 15 and over.

| Year | Average hourly wage | Average weekly wage |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | $46.96 | $1,773.90 |
| 2024 | $46.10 | $1,732.50 |
| 2023 | $44.82 | $1,703.37 |

- **Sources:** Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0064-01, Employee wages by industry, annual. The hourly series is v2292826 and the weekly series is v2292827. The reference period is 2025, released 2026-01-09. Values are in current dollars.
- **Limitation:** The NAICS "Public administration" category covers federal, provincial and local governments. I couldn't find a table that isolates Alberta's provincial government alone. These figures are therefore for all public administration in Alberta, not only the provincial level.

The average total income of people aged 15 and over in Alberta was **$66,100 in 2024**. That is the latest year available, and the figure is in 2024 constant dollars. It averages only over people who reported income, so zeros are excluded.

- It was $66,300 in 2023 and $66,000 in 2022.
- Over 2013–2024 the yearly figures ranged from $65,600 to $72,700.

Source: Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0239-01, vector v107680657. The series is Alberta; 15 years and over; total gender; total income; average income (excluding zeros). It was released 2026-04-29.

This is an average, which is pulled up by high earners. For a typical person, use the median instead. It is available in the same table (statistic 5) but I didn't retrieve it.

Alberta's median total income was **$96,600** in 2024, the latest year available. The figure is in 2024 constant dollars.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, table 11-10-0190-01, vector v96414571. The series is "Alberta; Median total income; Economic families and persons not in an economic family". It was released 2026-04-29.
- **Caveat:** This table measures income per economic family or unattached person, not per household, so it is the closest official match to "household income".
- **Recent years:** The median was $98,400 in 2023 and $96,700 in 2022, in 2024 constant dollars.
